description: National Water Model is a model or estimator listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by NOAA, National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration; National Center for Atmospheric Research; Consortium of Universities for the Advancement of Hydrologic Sciences, Inc.. Emergency managers, reservoir operators, and other decision makers can consult the supercomputer-powered National Water Model for detailed forecasts of soil moisture, surface runoff, snow water equivalent, and other parameters. The National Water Model (NWM) uses data from more than 8,000 U.S. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Drought, Flooding – General. Assets: Agriculture and Food Supply, Critical Facilities, People, Property, Water Infrastructure – General. The listed link gives the source code or documentation; nothing was downloaded or run. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
